critique: The render clearly reads as a dense white blizzard on black, with strong depth layering and convincing forward motion between t1 and t4. The t1 frame has a good mix of fine snow and nearer flakes. By t4, however, several foreground particles become excessively large, soft, and blown-out—especially along the upper-right and lower-right—making the result feel more like fast camera-flight debris than consistently scaled snowfall. The depth motion is strong but slightly too aggressive over the short frame interval.

suggestions.why: Reduce the oversized, heavily blurred foreground discs while retaining the dense fine-snow field and depth variation.
Moderate the extreme Z-axis wind so flakes advance toward camera with a more controlled blizzard drift rather than rapidly blooming into oversized foreground blobs.
